answer: Trust propagates via bounded random walks on the attestation graph, making influence depend on attested paths rather than self-asserted identities. A Sybil cluster, even one labeled comet, ferrous, or island, must reach honest nodes across an external cut; low conductance means few crossing edges relative to cluster volume. Min-cut and transitivity bounds thus limit aggregate voting weight crossing that bottleneck, without counting internal Sybil links as independent trust.
